title: Radian and Degree Measures of a Subtended Central Angle
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: An arc of length s = 10\pi along a circle of radius r = 8 subtends a central angle \theta. Find both the radian measure and the degree measure of \theta.

steps.title: Express the Central Angle in Radians Using Arc Length and Radius
steps.explanation: Solve the arc length formula s = r*theta for the central angle theta in radians.
steps.why: The radian measure of a central angle is defined as the ratio of subtended arc length to radius.

steps.title: Substitute Given Values to Find Radian Measure
steps.explanation: Substitute s = 10*pi and r = 8 into the ratio and reduce the fraction by a factor of 2.
steps.why: Dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor 2 simplifies the exact radian measure.

steps.title: Convert the Radian Measure to Degrees
steps.explanation: Multiply the radian measure 5*pi/4 by the conversion factor 180^circ/pi. Cancel pi and evaluate 5 * 45^circ = 225^circ.
steps.why: One radian equals 180/pi degrees because pi radians equal 180 degrees.
